candidates.exact_span: For the purposes of this Part, significant noncompliance shall be determined based upon the more stringent of either criteria established at 40 CFR Part 403.8(f)(2)(viii) [rev. 10/14/05] or criteria established in the approved POTW pretreatment program.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether significant noncompliance is measured against federal 403.8(f)(2)(viii) criteria or the approved local pretreatment program—and which is more stringent—changes which industrial users must be listed as noncompliant and what evidence is expected for FY2025 monitoring/reporting and missing-evidence determinations.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall prepare annually a list of Industrial Users which during the preceding twelve months were in significant noncompliance with applicable pretreatment requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'preceding twelve months' and which users qualify as in significant noncompliance determines whether annual listing/reporting obligations were triggered during FY2025 and what documented noncompliance evidence should exist versus unresolved missing-evidence cases.

candidates.exact_span: An updated list of all significant industrial users and identify which Industrial Users are Non-Significant Categorical Industrial Users (NSCIUs) or Middle Tier CIUs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classification of facilities as SIUs, NSCIUs, or Middle Tier CIUs determines which pretreatment monitoring and reporting requirements attach to each user during FY2025 and whether absence of user-specific data reflects a documented no-requirement state or missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Industrial Users subject to categorical Pretreatment Standards that are subject to reduced monitoring and reporting requirements under 40 CFR 403.12(e)(2) & (3);
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a user falls within 403.12(e)(2) or (3) reduced monitoring changes which monitoring is required in FY2025 and whether reported measurements should be compared against full categorical limits or a reduced monitoring regime.

candidates.exact_span: Industrial Users subject to the following categorical Pretreatment Standards [Organic Chemicals, Plastics, and Synthetic Fibers (OCPSF) (40 CFR part 414), Petroleum Refining (40 CFR part 419), and Pesticide Chemicals (40 CFR part 455)] and for which the Control Authority has chosen to use the concentration-based standards rather than converting them to flow-based mass standards as allowed at 40 CFR 403.6(c)(6);
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applicability of OCPSF, petroleum refining, or pesticide categorical standards and the choice to retain concentration-based limits instead of flow-based mass limits changes which enforceable numeric limits apply to reported measurements and which monitoring basis governs compliance comparisons.

candidates.exact_span: Categorical Industrial Users subject to concentration-based standards for which the Control Authority has chosen to convert the concentration-based standards to equivalent mass limits, as allowed at 40 CFR 403.6(c)(5);
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the Control Authority elected mass-limit conversion under 403.6(c)(5) changes the form and value of enforceable numeric discharge limits used to evaluate whether reported measurements exceed applicable limits.

candidates.exact_span: General Control Mechanisms used for similar groups of SIUs along with the substantially similar types of operations and the types of wastes that are the same, for each separate General Control Mechanism, as allowed at 40 CFR 403.8(f)(1)(iii);
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether facilities are covered by a General Control Mechanism and whether their operations and wastes are 'substantially similar' and 'the same' affects which collective limits and monitoring obligations apply instead of individual SIU-specific requirements.
